rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the hard-hearted are doomed to complete worldly misguidance and severe afterlife punishment; he cites 13:33 for the worldly judgment.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أنه تعالى حكم على القاسية قلوبهم بحكم في الدنيا وبحكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face is the body's most honored member: it bears beauty, houses the senses, distinguishes people, and displays happiness or misery; “face” can also name a people's leader or a thing's true aspect.
rows.anchor: أن أشرف الأعضاء هو الوجه لأنه محل الحسن والصباحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people sacrifice every other limb to shield the face, shielding oneself only with the face signifies total inability to ward off punishment; al-Nābigha's mock exception of sword-notches means his people have no real flaw.
rows.anchor: لا جرم حسن جعل الاتقاء بالوجه كناية عن العجز عن الاتقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a person cast into Hell has his hands bound to his neck and can ward off the fire only with his face.
rows.anchor: الذي يلقى في النار يلقى مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه ولا يتهيأ له أن يتقي النار إلا بوجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer completes the comparison: one forced to ward off punishment with his face is not like someone safe from it; he cannot ward it off at all.
rows.anchor: جوابه محذوف وتقديره أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة كمن هو آمن من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sūʾ al-ʿadhāb” means the severity of punishment.
rows.anchor: وسوء العذاب شدته . ثم قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi connects the warning to 39:25: earlier peoples were punished for denial, and the same cause present among these people entails the same consequence.
rows.anchor: تدل على أنهم إنما أتاهم العذاب بسبب التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment came from a direction they did not imagine could bring harm, while they felt secure.
rows.anchor: من الجهة التي لا يحسبون ولا يخطر ببالهم أن الشر يأتيهم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi explains disgrace as humiliation, contempt, and abasement; punishment is complete when pain comes with degradation.
rows.anchor: العذاب التام هو أن يحصل فيه الألم مقرونا بالهوان والذل

words: ولعذاب الاخرة أكبر لو كانوا يعلمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment stored for the next life is greater than the worldly punishment and disgrace already described.
rows.anchor: فالعذاب المدخر لهم في يوم القيامة أكبر وأعظم من ذلك الذي وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says these descriptions are intended to frighten and warn.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من كل ذلك التخويف والترهيب

words: ولقد ضربنا للناس فى هاذا القرءان من كل مثل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God presented every kind of parable in the Qur'an so people might remember; Razi says the purpose is plain.
rows.anchor: ولقد ضربنا للناس فى هاذا القرءان من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون

words: ضربنا للناس فى هاذا القرءان من كل مثل
rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila infer that God's acts and rulings are directed toward purposes because God says He sets out parables for people.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة دلت الآية على أن أفعال الله وأحكامه معللة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila infer that God intends faith and knowledge for everyone: the parables aim to produce remembrance and understanding.
rows.anchor: ومشعر بأن المقصود من ضرب هذه الأمثال إرادة حصول التذكر والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur'an contains useful explanations and compelling proofs, Razi says God follows them by praising the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه البيانات النافعة والبينات الباهرة موجودة في القرآن

words: ضربنا للناس فى هاذا القرءان من كل مثل
rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: One argument for the Qur'an's createdness is that it was brought about for the purpose of making people remember, and what is brought for a purpose is originated.
rows.anchor: والشيء الذي يؤتى به لغرض آخر يكون محدثا

rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: A second createdness argument says its Arabic wording depends on Arab conventions, so it is originated through human linguistic usage.
rows.anchor: وما كان حصوله بسبب أوضاع العرب واصطلاحاتهم كان مخلوقا محدثا

rows.speaker: القائلون بحدوث القرآن
rows.claim: A third argument treats Qur'an as recitation: recitation is a verbal noun, hence an act and an object, and therefore originated.
rows.anchor: القراءة مصدر والمصدر هو المفعول المطلق فكان فعلا ومفعولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that all three createdness arguments concern letters and sounds, which are originated.
rows.anchor: نحمل كل هذه الوجوه على الحروف والأصوات وهي حادثة ومحدثة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses “Arabic” as an accusative circumstantial qualifier, meaning the Qur'an is in a state of Arabic clarity; it may instead be an accusative of praise.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج قوله : { عربيا } منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first attribute, Qur'an, means it is recited in prayer niches until the Resurrection; Razi links this to 15:9.
rows.anchor: والمراد كونه متلوا في المحاريب إلى قيام القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic attribute means that eloquent speakers cannot produce a counterpart; Razi cites the challenge in 17:88.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنه أعجز الفصحاء والبلغاء عن معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Without crookedness” means the Qur'an is free of contradiction, as 4:82 argues.
rows.anchor: والمراد براءته عن التناقض

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila use “so that they may be wary” as evidence that God's rulings are purposive.
rows.anchor: فالمعتزلة يتمسكون به في تعليل أحكام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering precedes piety: once people recall, understand, and grasp the Qur'an's meaning, they can practice avoidance.
rows.anchor: والسبب فيه أن التذكر متقدم على الاتقاء

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi presents the closing statements as the decisive conclusion: reminders and proofs benefit only those whom God singles out for guidance and success.
rows.anchor: هذا الفضل لا ينفع والبينات إلا إذا خص الله العبد بالهداية والتوفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is mighty and exacting in retribution is a threat to the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { أليس الله بعزيز ذى انتقام } تهديد للكفار

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's Ashʿarī associates cite the paired guidance statements for their doctrine that God creates acts and wills all events.
rows.anchor: أصحابنا يتمسكون في مسألة خلق الأعمال وإرادة الكائنات بقوله

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila cite the threat of retribution: if God created unbelief in people, punishing and threatening them would be unfitting.
rows.anchor: صحة مذهبهم في هاتين المسألتين بقوله : { أليس الله بعزيز ذى انتقام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi describes people who, in poverty or illness, appeal to God and believe only He can remove their distress.
rows.anchor: عند الوقوع في الضر الذي هو الفقر والمرض يفزعون إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When granted wealth or health, they credit their own earnings, effort, or medical treatment, contradicting their earlier appeal to God.
rows.anchor: زعم أنه إنما حصل ذلك بكسبه وبسبب جهده وجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is a test: gratitude is due when it arrives and patience when it departs, like gold tested by fire; most people miss this purpose.
rows.anchor: عند حصولها يجب الشكر ، وعند فواتها يجب الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the brief phrase a fluent, concise exposure of their disgraceful inconsistency in hardship and ease.
rows.anchor: قبح طريقتهم فيما هم عليه عند الشدة والرخاء بلفظة وجيزة فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ here follows the earlier account that they recoil from hearing about God alone but rejoice at mention of partners; it marks their immediate contradiction. The opening-sūra parallel uses wāw because it does not stress immediacy.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر بفاء التعقيب أنهم إذا وقعوا في الضر والبلاء

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The unnamed couplet denies that auspicious Jupiter or ill-omened Saturn determines outcomes, attributing decree to the Lord of heaven.
rows.anchor: فلا السعد يقضي به المشترى … ولا النحس يقضي علينا زحل

words: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After summarizing that every soul is repaid for its deeds in 39:70, Razi explains the punishment scene, then the reward scene, closing the sūra.
rows.anchor: شرح أحوال أهل القيامة على سبيل الإجمال

rows.speaker: ابن زيدان
rows.claim: Ibn Zaydān says the unbelievers are driven to Hell violently and by force.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيدان : سوق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم يكون بالعنف والدفع

rows.speaker: ابن زيدان
rows.claim: Ibn Zaydān's reading of forced driving is supported by 52:13, 107:2, and 19:86, which use language of pushing or driving.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { يوم يدعون إلى نار جهنم دعا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Zumar” means separate successive companies, one group following another.
rows.anchor: وأما الزمر ، فهي الأفواج المتفرقة بعض في أثر بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gates of Hell are opened when the unbelievers reach it.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أبواب جهنم إنما تفتح عند وصول أولئك إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gatekeepers mean messengers from the unbelievers' own human kind.
rows.anchor: يتلون عليكم ءايات ربكم وينذرونكم لقاء يومكم هاذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Meeting this day” means meeting the time of entering Hell, not the Resurrection Day; Arabic commonly uses “day” for a time of hardship.
rows.anchor: أراد لقاء وقتكم هذا وهو وقت دخولهم النار ، لا يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers admit that messengers did come and recite God's signs to them.
rows.anchor: فعند هذا تقول الكفار : بلى قد أتونا وتلوا علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads their response as admitting that the sentence of punishment has applied; one under that sentence cannot escape, so the blessed do not become wretched nor the wretched blessed.
rows.anchor: ومن حقت عليه كلمة العذاب فكيف يمكنه الخلاص من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exchange indicates there is no binding obligation before revealed law: the messengers' arrival leaves the punished with no excuse, which would be pointless if revelation were not a condition of liability.
rows.anchor: دلت الآية على أنه لا وجوب قبل مجيء الشرع

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that if entry followed only a fixed decree, the angels' rebuke of the arrogant would be pointless; they say entry is for arrogance toward prophets and rejection of their proofs.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لو كان دخولهم النار لأجل أنه حقت عليهم كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second possibility, no one actually prevented Pharaoh from killing Moses; Pharaoh feared that a miracle would stop him and expose his fear, so he blustered to conceal it from his followers.
rows.anchor: والاحتمال الثاني : أن أحدا ما منع فرعون من قتل موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's words “let him call his Lord” are mockery: he says he will kill Moses and dares him to call on his Lord for rescue.
rows.anchor: أما قوله { وليدع ربه } فإنما ذكره على سبيل الاستهزاء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads the yāʾ in “let me” with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: فتح ابن كثير الياء من قوله { ذرونى }

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr read the yāʾ in “I fear” with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وفتح نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو الياء من { إنى أخاف }

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: نافع وابن عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿAmr read with wāw and omit “or,” coordinating both outcomes: altering the religion and manifesting corruption.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عمرو { وإن يظهروا } بالواو وبحذف أو

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: الذين قرأوا بصيغة أو
rows.claim: Readers who retain “or” mean that one of the two outcomes must occur.
rows.anchor: والذين قرأوا بصيغة أو فمعناه أنه لا بد من وقع أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: قُرِئ
rows.claim: A reading with ḍamma on yāʾ, kasra on hāʾ, and accusative “corruption” makes the verb transitive: Moses would cause corruption to appear.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يظهر بضم الياء وكسر الهاء والفساد بالنصب على التعدية

words: أَوْ أَن يُظْهِرَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْفَسَادَ
rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read “or corruption appears” with fatḥa and nominative “corruption”; if Moses changes religion, its resulting corruption appears.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بلفظ أو يظهر بفتح الياء والهاء والفساد بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh alleges that Moses' success would corrupt religion or worldly order: Egyptians regarded their own religion as true, and Moses could gather followers, spark disputes, and stir up strife; religion comes first because people prize it above wealth.
rows.anchor: المقصود من هذا الكلام بيان السبب الموجب لقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses responds to Pharaoh's plot only by seeking God's protection, God raises a separate person to defend him and calm the crisis.
rows.anchor: ما زاد في دفع مكر فرعون وشره على الاستعاذة بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says from personal experience that when he entrusts a wrongdoer's threatened harm to God without confronting him, God sends unknown people to oppose the harm vigorously.
rows.anchor: كلما قصدني شرير بشر ولم أتعرض له وأكتفي بتفويض ذلك الأمر إلى الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported identification says the believer was Pharaoh's cousin, effectively a crown prince and chief of police.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنه كان ابن عم لله ، وكان جاريا مجرى ولي العهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second identification says he was a Copt among Pharaoh's people but not a relative.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان قبطيا من آل فرعون وما كان من أقاربه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third identification says he was an Israelite.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه كان من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi judges the first identification likelier because “āl” can mean kin and clan, citing the household of Lot in 54:34.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب لأن لفظ الآل يقع على القرابة والعشيرة

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet names three foremost believers: Ḥabīb al-Najjār, the believer from Pharaoh's household, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, whom it calls the best of them; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله أنه قال : ( الصديقون ثلاثة : حبيب النجار

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad says Abū Bakr was better than the believer from Pharaoh's household: Abū Bakr proclaimed faith openly, while that believer concealed it.
rows.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد أنه قال : كان أبو بكر خيرا من مؤمن آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Min” may modify “believer,” making the man a member of Pharaoh's household.
rows.anchor: لفظ من في قوله { من ءال فرعون } يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بقوله { مؤمن }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported parse attaches “min” to “conceals his faith,” but an objection says Arabic does not express concealing something from someone in this construction; 4:42 is cited.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن هذا الاحتمال غير جائز لأنه يقال كتمت من فلان كذا

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce the jīm in “rajul” with ḍamma; another reading has kasra, as in the two pronunciations of ʿuḍud.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : رجل مؤمن الأكثرون قرأوا بضم الجيم

words: أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّىَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is an emphatic denial: the man has only said his Lord is God and brought signs, neither of which warrants killing.
rows.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار ، وقد ذكر في هذا الكلام ما يدل على حسن ذلك الاستنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's phrase “my Lord is God” points to monotheism, while “clear proofs” refers to evidence for it, including Moses' statements in 20:50 and 26:24.
rows.anchor: قوله { ربى الله } إشارة إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer offers a dilemma: if Moses lies, the burden of his lie is on him; if he is truthful, some promised punishment will reach them, so either way they should leave him alive.
rows.anchor: كان وبال كذبه عائدا علليه فاتركوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says a liar's harm would spread beyond himself because followers might adopt his false religion and provoke conflict.
rows.anchor: أنا لا نسلم أن بتقدير كونه كاذبا

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Razi says scholars unanimously hold that a heretic who calls people to his heresy should be killed.
rows.anchor: ولهذا السبب العلماء أجمعوا على أن الزنديق الذي يدعو الناس إلى زندقته يجب قتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection says that if this reasoning were sound, every liar could use it to defend a false religion.
rows.anchor: إن كان الكلام حجة له ، فلا كذاب إلا ويمكنه أن يتمسك بهذه الطريقة

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection says the reasoning would also forbid rejecting opponents of Moses: if their denial were false, its burden would be theirs, and if true, others could benefit.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن الكفار الذين أنكروا نبوة موسى عليه السلام وجب أن لا يجوز الإنكار عليهم

words: وَإِن يَكُ صَادِقًۭا يُصِبْكُم بَعْضُ ٱلَّذِى يَعِدُكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection asks why the believer says “some” of what Moses promises: soothsayers may partly predict events, but a prophet speaking revelation should be wholly truthful.
rows.anchor: كان من الواجب أن يقال وإن يك صادقا يصبكم كل الذي يعدكم لأن الذي يصيب في بعض ما يعد دون البعض هم أصحاب الكهانة والنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers the objections together: killing is unnecessary; they can stop Moses from publicly preaching and leave him alive, so a liar's harm stays with him while a truthful man's message can benefit them.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة بكم في دفع شره إلى قتله بل يكفيكم أن تمنعوه عن إظهار هذه المقالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Some” is a fair minimum: if Moses lies, the harm is his; if he is truthful, at least some warning reaches them, which presents the case without obstinacy.
rows.anchor: مدار هذا الاستدلال على إظهار الإنصاف وترك اللجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses threatened worldly and afterlife punishment; the arrival of worldly punishment would count as some of what he promised.
rows.anchor: كان يتوعدهم بعذاب الدنيا وبعذاب الآخرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says “some” may mean “all,” citing Labīd's verse about death catching up with some souls.
rows.anchor: حكي عن أبي عبيدة أنه قال ورود لفظ البعض بمعنى الكل جائز

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority rejects Abū ʿUbayda's usage as mistaken, saying Labīd meant himself by “some souls.”
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أن هذا القول خطأ ، قالوا وأراد لبيد ببعض النفوس نفسه

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer alludes that God guided Moses to manifest miracles, and one so guided cannot be a profligate liar; this indirectly exalts Moses and denies that he lies.
rows.anchor: ومن هداه الله إلى الإتيان بالمعجزات لا يكون مسرفا كذابا فهذا يدل على أن موسى عليه السلام ليس من الكاذبين

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَنْ هُوَ مُسْرِفٌۭ كَذَّابٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may describe Pharaoh as profligate in resolving to kill Moses and lying by claiming divinity; God will frustrate and destroy his power.
rows.anchor: أن فرعون مسرف في عزمة على قتل موسى
